title.narrative: ROAf Cameroon: Technical Support to improve Hygiene in 158 Health Facilities through the Construction of Boreholes and the Establishment of Participatory Management Systems in Beneficiary Municipalities in Cameroon.

description.narrative: The National AIDS Control Committee (CNLS in French) is the body in charge of coordinating and managing the National AIDS Control Program throughout the country in collaboration with the government and national and international partners. The experience gained by the CNLS through its multiple successful interventions related to managing the spread of HIV-AIDS in Cameroon has enabled the CNLS to draw the attention of the national response committee to COVID-19 and of public and international opinion to the importance of putting in place simple but effective barrier measures through access to water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) services. Following a call for expressions of interest from the Global Fund, the CNLS formulated a project proposal that was allocated funding for the construction of 158 boreholes in the communes and health facilities in Cameroon, a project that should support the response plan against COVID-19 already initiated by the Cameroonian government and whose results are already visible. This proposal was developed in liaison with the Water and Sanitation team of the Urban Basic Service Unit. In a context of permanent lack of potable water supply in several health facilities, notably the Integrated Health Centres (IHCs) in Cameroon, there is a lack of respect for barrier measures such as systematic hand washing on entering and leaving health facilities. This is compounded by the poor maintenance capacity of existing wells in some IHCs, often preventing them from providing the service for which they were built. The need of installation of a permanent and easily accessible source of drinking water in the IHCs along with an effective maintenance plan of wells over their service life, are therefore urgent. Based on that, the CNLS plans to construct 158 drinking water wells in the communes and health facilities (FOSA in French) throughout the 10 regions of Cameroon, with financing from the Global Fund. It also plans capacity-building sessions on the management and maintenance techniques of the wells that will be installed, as well as awareness-raising on the measures to be taken around the water points to be installed. UN-Habitat will mainly contribute to the planning and organisation of the contracting process, and will ensure supervision, monitoring and reporting to the CNLS. Furthermore, UN-Habitat will produce a final technical and financial report. By supporting this initiative, the CNLS and UN-Habitat intend to contribute to the reduction of the negative socio-economic effects of COVID-19 in the municipalities in general and the Health facilities in particular.
